arc.scene1_hook: A figure stands on a blank stage — no props, no labels, no instructions. A spotlight hits them. They pick up a pen and begin drawing their own path on the ground. It's exhilarating — curves, spirals, whatever they want. True self-definition. Then they turn around to face others standing in darkness and say: "Now you do this too." A commandment. On a blank stage dedicated to having no commandments. Title pill: "YOU CAN'T COMMAND FREEDOM".
arc.scene2_mystery: The figure continues drawing their path — it's beautiful, personal, unique. Other figures watch from the edges, impressed. The existential proposition visualized: existence precedes essence. You arrive without a script. Meaning is not discovered — it's made. A hand shapes clay into a personal trophy — not the standard gold one, but something organic, unique. "YOU DECIDE WHAT COUNTS" label glows. The liberation is enormous. And it is real.
arc.scene3_wrong_answer: The assumption: if imposed metrics are bad, personal metrics solve everything. The standard gold yardstick gets replaced by a colorful handmade one — same function, new paint. The figure measures with their personal yardstick proudly. "MY METRICS" label in warm colors. It feels revolutionary. You've personalized success. But notice: you haven't eliminated measurement. You've just changed whose name is on the ruler. The question: is a private yardstick any less a yardstick?
arc.scene4_contradiction: The figure with the personal yardstick turns to help others. They hold up their self-made path and say "DEFINE YOURSELF!" — but this instruction appears as a stone tablet, glowing with authority. A commandment. The contradiction visualized: prescribing self-determination IS a commandment against commandments. The stone tablet cracks down the middle. Two halves: "BE FREE" on one, "BECAUSE I SAID SO" on the other. The existentialist gets tangled — should we help others define themselves? That's a prescription. The paradox is inescapable.
arc.scene5_proof: A logic chain descends the screen. Step 1: "Imposed meaning → bad" (red X). Step 2: "Make your own meaning → good" (green check). Step 3: "Tell others to make their own meaning" — the green check glitches and turns into a red X. Because Step 3 IS Step 1 wearing different clothes. A mirror visual: the existentialist's commandment reflects and shows the same structure as the original imposed framework. A feedback loop arrow circles endlessly. The moment you turn around and say "follow me," you have left the path.
arc.scene6_betrayal: The figure who drew their own path looks back — and sees footprints behind them. Others followed. The unique personal path has become a highway. The existentialist's dilemma: their liberation became a doctrine, their freedom became a franchise. The blank stage from Scene 1 now has a neon sign: "AUTHENTIC SELF-EXPRESSION (REQUIRED)". The figure stands alone again, realizing: the way that can be spoken is not the eternal way. You can point, but pointing isn't commanding. You can walk your path, but the moment you say "follow me," you've left it.

tts_script: If success can't be accepted as given, and can't be simply rejected, maybe it can be reclaimed. The existential proposition: existence precedes essence. You arrive without a script. Meaning isn't discovered, it's made. You get to define your own success. The liberation is enormous. And real. But notice what happened. You haven't eliminated measurement. You've personalized it. You still measure, just by your own instrument now. And here's the uncomfortable question: is a private yardstick any less a yardstick? Worse — if you tell others to define success for themselves, that's a commandment against commandments. A prescription against prescriptions. The moment you turn around and say follow me, you have left the path.
